E1.cap: Table E.1. Alpha sweep of the target-calibrated split-conformal intervals (same-protocol recomputation batch).
E1.note: Note: mean ± std over 5 seeds; PICP = empirical coverage; NMPIW = MPIW divided by the mean true SOH of the test windows; Winkler score at the nominal level (lower is better); Pinball = mean of the alpha/2 and 1-alpha/2 quantile losses (lower is better); NMPIW and Winkler shrink as alpha grows because the intervals narrow. Protocol and drift analysis in Appendix E.1; CSV: results_p0/p0_2_metrics.csv.

E2.cap: Table E.2. Paired statistics of fine-tuned model versus persistence baseline (five per-seed pooled RMSEs).
E2.note: Note: dz = paired Cohen's d on the per-seed RMSE differences (positive = model worse than persistence); exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank; Holm-Bonferroni within the eight-comparison family; the zero-shot family (all dz between +2.55 and +11.70, all p = 0.0625, 0 wins in all 40 seed-domain-backbone runs) is tabulated in the supplementary CSV. With n = 5 paired samples the smallest attainable two-sided p is 0.0625. Pooling caveat: the per-seed persistence RMSEs here are pooled over test windows within each run (same pooling as the model column; CALCE/TCN H = 10 gives 0.0715-0.0966 per seed), whereas the single-value persistence of Table 3 pools all cells (0.0832); the two differ at the second decimal.

E3.cap: Table E.3. Computational cost of the four backbones (RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, 8 GB, CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.11).
E3.note: Note: one source-domain fit per backbone under the protocol of Section 3.2 (early stopping patience 10, cap 120 epochs); the wall-clock reflects each architecture's own early-stopping draw, consistent with the budget caveat of Table 2; inference latency averaged over 100 forward passes after warm-up on GPU.

E4.cap: Table E.4. Uncertainty baselines versus target-calibrated conformal intervals (alpha = 0.10, identical splits and seeds).
E4.note: Note: mean ± std over 5 seeds (42-46; the ensemble uses the seed-42 split with five initialisations, a single split by cost); nominal coverage 0.90; the conformal row is the TCN subset of the recomputation batch of Table E.1 at alpha = 0.10 (five seeds), matching the TCN backbone of the baseline rows; ensemble intervals are mean ± z_{0.95} times the member standard deviation, MC dropout uses 30 train-mode sampling passes, quantile regression outputs the tau = 0.1/0.9 heads directly. CSV: results_p0/p0_1_uncertainty.csv.

E5.cap: Table E.5. Window (W) and horizon (H) sensitivity of the fine-tuned transfer (five-seed mean ± std RMSE).
E5.note: Note: W sensitivity (W = 10/30/40 versus the main W = 20) retrains the source model per window length under the protocol of Section 3.2; the LSTM horizon rows extend the horizon sensitivity of Section 4.3 (the TCN H = 5/20 rows come from the archived transfer_sens runs of the same anchor). The persistence column repeats the H-matched pooled baseline of Table 3 for reading off whether the fine-tuned model beats it at each setting.
